Reasoning:

1. The singlet at 2.1 ppm (3 H, s) is typical for the –OCOCH₃ methyl of an acetate ester.

2. The doublet at 1.6 ppm (3 H, d, J ≈ 7 Hz) is a methyl group coupled to a single neighboring proton (a vinyl CH).

3. The signal at 5.5 ppm (1 H, dq) couples to both the 3-H methyl (J ≈ 7 Hz) and another vinylic proton with J ≈ 16 Hz.  
   • Thus it is a vinyl CH adjacent to a CH₃ group and trans-coupled (J ≈ 16 Hz) to another vinyl proton.

4. The 7.0 ppm resonance (1 H, d, J ≈ 16 Hz) is the other vinylic proton, trans to the one at 5.5 ppm.

5. Only four distinct proton environments are seen; importantly, no CH₂ signal near 4 ppm is present. Therefore there is no –CH₂–O– group, ruling out a butenyl acetate (which would contain an O-CH₂ group).

6. The data match an acetate of the type CH₃–CH=CH–OCOCH₃ with the double bond in the trans configuration: trans-propenyl acetate.

Hence the unknown compound is trans-propenyl acetate.

Answer: B
